academicDiscussion.professorPost: Airports have traditionally reserved airline lounge access for travelers with premium tickets or elite status. Recently, some airports have begun selling day passes that let any traveler, regardless of ticket class, pay to use a lounge for a single visit. What do you think? Should lounge access be opened to any paying traveler, or should it stay reserved for premium ticket holders? Why or why not?

studentPosts.name: Maya
studentPosts.post: I think day passes make sense. If someone is willing to pay for a quiet place to work or rest between flights, why should their ticket class decide whether they can? Airlines already sell extra comfort separately, like seat upgrades, so letting anyone buy lounge access just extends that same idea to a different service.

studentPosts.name: Owen
studentPosts.post: I get Maya's point about paying for comfort, but I think day passes ruin what makes lounges valuable in the first place. Premium travelers already pay more for their tickets partly because of that quieter space, and once day passes are sold widely, lounges get crowded and noisy, so the benefit premium passengers paid extra for basically disappears.
